newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shenzhen B index ends up at 1997 high.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen B index ends up at 1997 high.

text.p: Shenzhen's B index closed on Monday at its highest level this year for the third straight session due to heavy buying of large capitalisation companies by investors despite some profit-taking, analysts said.

The foreign currency B index rose 0.69 points or 0.38 percent to end at 181.79 on turnover of HK$368.4 million, after reaching 1997-highs on Friday and Thursday as well. Turnover was HK$440.6 million last Friday.
Heavy buying in Wafangdian Bearing Co lifted the index, which has also been supported by the recent reporting of strong economic indicators, one analyst said.
"Wafangdian is an attractive new index-weighted stock," an analyst at J&A Securities said.
Wafangdian soared HK$0.64 or 9.98 percent to end at HK$7.05, making it the second best performer today.
It was also the most actively traded stock on volume of 8.39 million shares.
"The price/earnings ratio (of Wafangdian) is low compared to other B shares and investors tend to favour new shares," the J&A Securities analyst said.

The company, the only firm to be listed on the Shenzhen B share market so far in 1997, posted earnings per share of 0.50 yuan for the January-September period of 1996 against 0.47 yuan for the whole of 1995, based on Chinese accounting standards.
Conglomerate China Vanke Co was the sharpest gainer today, adding HK$0.78 to reach its 10 percent limit-up and close at HK$8.58.
Analysts said the B index has been rising due to favorable economic data released by Beijing last week.
China expects to record gross domestic product growth (GDP) of 10 percent in 1997 with retail price inflation staying below five percent, the State Statistical Bureau said on Friday.
The A share index rose 9.54 points or 2.06 percent to 471.50 on turnover of 12.26 billion yuan against Friday's 8.46 billion.
Shenzhen Development Bank, which released strong annual results on Monday, was the star among the A shares, gaining 2.16 yuan or 7.47 percent to close at 31.09 yuan on volume of 36.73 million.
"Profit-taking set in, but the buying momentum still pushed the index ahead," said an analyst at China Guotai Securities.
The index hit an intraday low of 178.63 points but many investors held on, analysts said.
The index is likely to move higher in the next few sessions judging by the recent heavy trading volume, they said.
"The index may break through the 200-point barrier in the short- to medium-term as funds are still pouring in," the Guotai analyst said.
